Questions.Question: How many players can a club put on its main squad list?
How many places in the main squad list are reserved for locally trained players, and how many of those can be association-trained?
Questions.Answer: According to Article 31.04, a total of eight places in the main squad list (List A) are reserved exclusively for locally trained players. Out of these eight places, no more than four can be filled by association-trained players.

Questions.Question: A club registers a new player during the qualifying phase and that takes List A to 26 names. What must it do?
Questions.Answer: If a club registers a new player during the qualifying phase and that takes List A to 26 names, the club must remove one previously registered player from List A to reduce the total number to 25. This is required by regulation 31.10, which mandates that if the number of players on List A exceeds 25, the club must reduce the list by removing the necessary number of players previously registered.

Questions.Question: What is the minimum number of goalkeepers a club must register?
What are the age and tenure conditions for putting a young player on List B?
Can a club add new players to its squad after the league phase ends?
Questions.Answer: Yes, after the completion of the league phase and before the start of the knockout phase, a club may register a maximum of three new eligible players for the remaining matches in the current competition. Such registrations must be completed by 5 February 2026 (24:00 CET) at the latest (Paragraph 32.01). Additionally, in specific exceptional cases outlined in Paragraph 32.02, clubs might be entitled to register additional players (beyond three), depending on the number of players no longer registered with the club after the league phase.

Questions.Question: How many substitutions is a team allowed during a match?
Questions.Answer: A team is allowed up to five substitutions during a match, with an additional sixth substitution permitted exclusively during extra time in knockout matches. Each team may use a maximum of three stoppages in play to make these substitutions, with one additional stoppage allowed in extra time. Substitutions made before the start of the match, during half-time, between the end of normal playing time and extra time, and at half-time during extra time do not count towards these stoppages.

Questions.Question: What happens if a knockout tie is level after both legs?
What share of stadium capacity has to be made available to visiting supporters, and is there a price limit?
Questions.Answer: According to regulation [45.01], the home club must make at least 5% of the spectator capacity of the stadium available to visiting supporters. The ticket prices for visiting supporters cannot exceed the price paid by home supporters for adult tickets in a comparable sector of the stadium. Additionally, in no case shall the price of tickets for visiting supporters exceed €50.

Questions.Question: How many medals do the winning and losing finalists receive?
Questions.Answer: According to Paragraph 11.03 of the regulations, the winning team in the UEFA Champions League final is presented with 50 gold medals, and the losing team is presented with 50 silver medals.

Questions.Question: If a club only has six locally trained players available, what happens to the size of its squad?
Two clubs finish the league phase on the same number of points. How is the higher position decided?
A player is sent off in the last league phase match. Does that suspension carry into the knockout rounds?
Questions.Answer: Yes, a player sent off in the last league phase match is suspended for the next match in the UEFA Champions League, which would include the first knockout round match. According to paragraph 63.01, a player sent off is automatically suspended for the next match in a UEFA club competition.

Questions.Question: A club's first-choice goalkeeper is injured for two months. Can they bring in a replacement, and does the replacement have to be locally trained?
Questions.Answer: Yes, a club can bring in a replacement goalkeeper if the first-choice goalkeeper is injured and the injury is considered long-term (lasting at least 30 days). The replacement goalkeeper does not have to be locally trained, even if the injured goalkeeper was. This is specified in Paragraph [31.14(aa)].

Questions.Question: How long must an outfield player be out before he can be replaced, and is that the same threshold as for a goalkeeper?
Questions.Answer: An outfield player must be out for at least 60 days due to long-term injury or illness before he can be replaced (Paragraph 31.14 cc). For a goalkeeper, the threshold is at least 30 days due to long-term injury or illness (Paragraph 31.14 aa). Therefore, the thresholds for replacement are not the same for outfield players and goalkeepers.

Questions.Question: Two clubs turn up with clashing shirts. Who has to change — and is the answer different in the final?
Can two clubs owned by the same investment group both play in this competition?
Questions.Answer: No, two clubs owned by the same investment group cannot both participate in the UEFA Champions League simultaneously. According to regulation [5.01], no individual or legal entity may have control or influence over more than one club participating in a UEFA club competition. Control or influence is defined as holding a majority of the shareholders’ voting rights, appointing or removing a majority of administrative officers, having a controlling agreement with other shareholders, or exercising decisive influence over the club’s decision-making.

Questions.Question: A match is abandoned at half-time and resumed the following day. Which players can take the field?
Does a player's passport determine whether he counts toward the domestic development requirement?
Questions.Answer: No, a player's passport does not determine whether he counts toward the domestic development requirement. Instead, the criteria for being a domestic (locally trained) player are based on the player's registration history between the ages of 15 and 21. Specifically, to qualify as a 'club-trained player,' the player must have been registered with the current club for at least three full seasons or 36 months during that period (Paragraph 31.06). Similarly, to qualify as an 'association-trained player,' the player must have been registered with clubs within the same association for at least three full seasons or 36 months during the same period (Paragraph 31.07). Nationality and passport are not factors in these definitions.

Questions.Question: A player left off both squad lists picks up a ban. Can he sit it out while unregistered?
After a defeat, is the head coach personally required to speak to broadcasters, and how quickly must the press conference start?
Questions.Answer: Yes, the head coach is personally required to speak to broadcasters after a defeat. The post-match press conference must start no later than 20 minutes after the final whistle (paragraph 80.02).

Questions.Question: Can a club choose which ball is used for its home fixtures?
Questions.Answer: No, a club cannot choose which ball is used for its home fixtures. According to paragraph 50.02 of the UEFA Champions League regulations, the official UEFA Champions League match ball, as determined by the UEFA administration, must be used for all matches from the play-offs onwards, as well as for the official training sessions before these matches.

Questions.Question: Does Liverpool's registered squad satisfy the locally trained player requirement?
Questions.Answer: Liverpool's registered squad does not satisfy the locally trained player requirement outlined in UEFA Champions League regulations. Per regulation 31.04, a minimum of eight players on List A must be designated as 'locally trained,' and no club may have more than four 'association-trained' players in these eight slots. Liverpool's squad includes only five locally trained players (three club-trained and two association-trained), which is below the required minimum of eight.

Questions.Question: Manchester United are short on club-trained players. How many can they actually register on List A as things stand?
Questions.Answer: Manchester United currently have 3 club-trained players in their squad. According to paragraph 31.08, if a club has fewer than eight locally trained players on List A (a combination of club-trained and association-trained players), the maximum number of players that can be registered on List A is reduced accordingly. Manchester United have 8 locally trained players (3 club-trained and 5 association-trained). Therefore, they can register the full 25 players on List A despite being short on club-trained players, as the total number of locally trained players meets the requirement.

Questions.Question: Real Madrid have registered the goalkeepers shown in their squad. Are they compliant on that front?
Questions.Answer: Yes, Real Madrid are compliant regarding their goalkeepers as they have registered two goalkeepers on their squad list, as required by the regulation in paragraph 31.13.
